_about: Title, hint and (where rewritten) explanation for every assessed Maths question, read by scripts/build_maths_content.py (teacher review 5: one hint per unit, "Maths discovery N" titles, "... is the answer." explanations). Keys are book question IDs. Since 21 October 2026 also the 15 former "Try it at home" questions and the worksheet questions (IDs with .sheet.). Since 23 October 2026 also class-book topics the companion leaves out (IDs with .book.).

math.u01.main.01.title: Counting apples
math.u01.main.01.hint: Touch each apple once and say one number for each.
math.u01.main.01.home: Put 8 apples or oranges in a row. Your child touches each one and says one number for each.

math.u01.main.02.title: Counting stars
math.u01.main.02.hint: Touch each star once. Keep going until every star is counted.
math.u01.main.02.home: Draw 13 stars spread out on paper. Your child ticks each star as it is counted, so none is missed.

math.u01.main.03.title: Number track gaps
math.u01.main.03.hint: Say the numbers in order. Which one is missing between its neighbours?
math.u01.main.03.home: Write 11 to 20 on a paper strip and cover a few numbers. Your child says the missing numbers.

math.u01.main.04.title: Dot pictures
math.u01.main.04.hint: Count the dots in each picture, one dot at a time.
math.u01.main.04.home: Draw dot cards for 4, 6 and 10, and write the numbers on other cards. Your child matches each dot card to its number.

math.u01.main.06.title: Spreading out
math.u01.main.06.hint: Were any cups added or taken away, or only moved?
math.u01.main.06.home: Put 6 cups close together and count them. Spread them out across the table and count again: still 6.

math.u01.main.07.title: Writing twelve
math.u01.main.07.hint: Twelve is ten and two more. Look for a 1 and then a 2.
math.u01.main.07.home: Write 12, 21 and 2 on cards. Say "twelve" and ask your child to pick the right card: a 1, then a 2.

math.u01.choice.01.title: The last number
math.u01.choice.01.hint: Count three things aloud. What does your last number tell you?
math.u01.choice.01.explanation: The last number you say tells how many there are altogether.
math.u01.choice.01.home: Count 5 shoes together. Ask "How many shoes?" and help your child answer with the last number said.

math.u01.choice.02.title: Just after 15
math.u01.choice.02.hint: Say 15, then say the next counting number.
math.u01.choice.02.explanation: Counting on one step from 15 gives 16.
math.u01.choice.02.home: Count up the stairs or along a ruler. Stop at 15 and ask which number comes just after.

math.u01.choice.03.title: A full ten frame
math.u01.choice.03.hint: Count the empty spaces in the ten frame.
math.u01.choice.03.explanation: A ten frame has 10 spaces, so 10 dots fill it.
math.u01.choice.03.home: Draw a ten frame (2 rows of 5 boxes). Put a dot in each box and count: a full frame holds 10.

math.u01.choice.04.title: Writing thirteen
math.u01.choice.04.hint: Thirteen is ten and three. Which digit comes first?
math.u01.choice.04.explanation: Thirteen is one ten and three ones, so we write 13.
math.u01.choice.04.home: Write 13, 31 and 30 on cards. Say "thirteen" and your child picks 13: a ten and three.

math.u01.choice.05.title: Spoons in a line
math.u01.choice.05.hint: Were any spoons added or taken away?
math.u01.choice.05.explanation: Only their places changed, so there are still 5 spoons.
math.u01.choice.05.home: Put 5 spoons in a pile and count them. Lay them in a long line and count again: still 5.

math.u02.main.01.title: One more, one less
math.u02.main.01.hint: One more is the next number; one less is the number before.
math.u02.main.01.home: Build a tower of 6 blocks. Add one and count. Then start with 10 and take one away.

math.u02.main.02.title: Counting on
math.u02.main.02.hint: Start on 5, then make three jumps forward.
math.u02.main.02.home: Draw a number line from 0 to 10. Your child puts a finger on 5 and makes 3 jumps forward.

math.u02.main.03.title: Counting back
math.u02.main.03.hint: Start on 9, then make four jumps back.
math.u02.main.03.home: On the same number line, start at 9 and make 4 jumps back, saying each number.

math.u02.main.04.title: Adding two groups
math.u02.main.04.hint: Count the blue dots, then the orange dots. Do the groups join?
math.u02.main.04.home: Put 4 spoons and 3 forks together and count them all. Then write 4 + 3 = 7 and read it aloud.

math.u02.main.05.title: Taking away cubes
math.u02.main.05.hint: Count 8 cubes, cover 3, then count the cubes left.
math.u02.main.05.home: Put 8 blocks in a line and take 3 away. Your child counts how many remain.

math.u02.main.06.title: Words and signs
math.u02.main.06.hint: Add means +, take away means −, and equals means =.
math.u02.main.06.home: Tell a short story ("4 birds, and 3 more come") and help your child write it as 4 + 3 = 7. Then try a take-away story.

math.u02.main.07.title: Cars drive away
math.u02.main.07.hint: Do the cars join the group or leave it?
math.u02.main.07.home: Park 8 toy cars and drive 4 away. Your child says the take-away sentence: 8 − 4 = 4.

math.u02.main.08.title: How many more
math.u02.main.08.hint: Pair each of Ali's sweets with one of Mona's.
math.u02.main.08.home: Make a line of 7 spoons with a line of 4 underneath. Your child counts the spoons that have no partner.

math.u02.choice.01.title: Picture of 2 + 3
math.u02.choice.01.explanation: 2 + 3 means 2 and 3 more put together: 5 in all.
math.u02.choice.01.home: Put 2 apples on a plate and add 3 more. Talk about how plus puts the groups together: 5 in all.

math.u02.choice.02.title: Take away 2
math.u02.choice.02.hint: Start on 6 and jump back twice.
math.u02.choice.02.explanation: Two jumps back from 6 land on 4.
math.u02.choice.02.home: Hold up 6 fingers and fold down 2. Count the fingers still up.

math.u02.choice.03.title: Jumping to take away
math.u02.choice.03.hint: Taking away makes a number smaller. Where are the smaller numbers?
math.u02.choice.03.explanation: Taking away makes numbers smaller, so we jump backwards.
math.u02.choice.03.home: Walk along the floor tiles: forwards when you add, backwards when you take away.

math.u02.choice.04.title: One less than 8
math.u02.choice.04.hint: Say the number that comes just before 8.
math.u02.choice.04.home: Put 8 cups in a row, take one away and count. Practise "one less" with other numbers too.

math.u02.choice.05.title: Adding zero
math.u02.choice.05.hint: Zero means nothing. What happens when you add nothing?
math.u02.choice.05.explanation: Adding zero adds nothing, so 5 stays 5.
math.u02.choice.05.home: Put 5 spoons on one plate and nothing on another. Put the plates together: adding zero changes nothing.

math.u03.main.01.title: Naming flat shapes
math.u03.main.01.hint: Count the straight sides and the corners of each shape.
math.u03.main.01.home: Find a circle, a triangle, a square and a rectangle at home (a plate, half a sandwich, a tile, a door). Name each shape together.

math.u03.main.02.title: Shape riddle
math.u03.main.02.hint: Which shapes have 4 corners? Which one has all its sides the same?
math.u03.main.02.home: Measure the sides of a square tile or paper with a piece of string. Your child checks that all 4 sides are the same.

math.u03.main.03.title: Solid riddle
math.u03.main.03.hint: Think of a dice and count its square faces.
math.u03.main.03.home: Hold a dice or a cube-shaped box. Count its square faces, then its corners, together.

math.u03.main.04.title: Triangle facts
math.u03.main.04.hint: Touch each side of a triangle, then each corner.
math.u03.main.04.home: Make a triangle with 3 straws or pencils on the table. Count the sides, then the corners.

math.u03.main.05.title: Shapes that roll
math.u03.main.05.hint: A shape with a curved surface can roll.
math.u03.main.05.home: Gently roll a ball, a tin, a box and a dice on the floor. Sort them: rolls or does not roll.

math.u03.main.06.title: Flat or solid
math.u03.main.06.hint: Could you hold it and turn it in your hand?
math.u03.main.06.home: Put solid things (a tin, a ball, a box) next to their outlines drawn on paper. Talk about which ones you can hold and which are flat.

math.u03.main.07.title: Turning a square
math.u03.main.07.hint: Count its sides and corners after turning. Did they change?
math.u03.main.07.home: An adult cuts a paper square. Turn it onto a corner and check together: still 4 equal sides and 4 corners.

math.u03.choice.01.title: A football
math.u03.choice.01.hint: Is a football flat or solid? Is it round all over?
math.u03.choice.01.explanation: A football is solid and round all over, like a sphere.
math.u03.choice.01.home: Hold a football and an orange. Your child feels that they are round all over: both are spheres.

math.u03.choice.02.title: A cereal box
math.u03.choice.02.hint: Are all its faces squares, or are some long rectangles?
math.u03.choice.02.explanation: A cereal box has rectangle faces, so it is a cuboid.
math.u03.choice.02.home: Look at a cereal or tissue box. Count its faces together and see that some are long rectangles: it is a cuboid.

math.u03.choice.03.title: Rectangle corners
math.u03.choice.03.hint: Touch each corner of a rectangle and count.
math.u03.choice.03.explanation: A rectangle has four corners, like a door.
math.u03.choice.03.home: Draw round a book on paper. Your child counts the corners of the rectangle: 4.

math.u03.choice.04.title: No corners
math.u03.choice.04.hint: Run your finger round each shape. Which one never turns a corner?
math.u03.choice.04.explanation: A circle is round all the way, so it has no corners.
math.u03.choice.04.home: Draw round a cup and a box. Run a finger round each shape and find the one with no corners.

math.u03.choice.05.title: A print in sand
math.u03.choice.05.hint: Look at the flat end of a tin. What shape is it?
math.u03.choice.05.explanation: The flat end of a tin is a circle.
math.u03.choice.05.home: Press the bottom of a tin into play dough or sand, then lift it. Your child names the shape of the print.

math.u04.main.01.title: Counting votes
math.u04.main.01.hint: Find the apple row and count its pictures once.
math.u04.main.01.home: Ask each family member for a favourite fruit and put one spoon in that fruit's row. Count the apple row.

math.u04.main.02.title: The favourite
math.u04.main.02.hint: Which row has the most pictures?
math.u04.main.02.home: Look at your spoon chart. Your child finds the longest row: that fruit is the favourite.

math.u04.main.03.title: The fewest
math.u04.main.03.hint: Which row has the fewest pictures?
math.u04.main.03.home: In the same chart, find the shortest row: the fruit the fewest people chose.

math.u04.main.04.title: Two rows together
math.u04.main.04.hint: Count the banana pictures, then count on the orange ones.
math.u04.main.04.home: Count the banana row and the orange row, then count both rows together.

math.u04.main.05.title: Everyone asked
math.u04.main.05.hint: Count every picture in every row once.
math.u04.main.05.home: Count every spoon in the chart: one spoon for each person asked.

math.u04.main.06.title: Sorting by colour
math.u04.main.06.hint: Ask one question about each toy: is it red?
math.u04.main.06.home: Sort a few toys into two groups: red and not red. Your child explains where each toy goes and why.

math.u04.main.07.title: Pet votes
math.u04.main.07.hint: Count how many children chose each pet.
math.u04.main.07.home: Ask family and friends which pet they like and draw one line for each answer: cat, dog or fish. Count each total.

math.u04.choice.01.title: The picture key
math.u04.choice.01.hint: Read the key under the pictogram.
math.u04.choice.01.explanation: The key says each picture shows one person.
math.u04.choice.01.home: Make a picture chart where each drawing is one person. Your child points to a drawing and says who it stands for.

math.u04.choice.02.title: The longest row
math.u04.choice.02.hint: More pictures make a row longer.
math.u04.choice.02.explanation: The longest row has the most pictures, so it shows the most.
math.u04.choice.02.home: Make two rows of cups for two drinks the family likes. The longer row shows the drink most people chose.

math.u04.choice.03.title: Block graphs
math.u04.choice.03.hint: Look at what each column is built from.
math.u04.choice.03.explanation: A block graph is built from equal square blocks.
math.u04.choice.03.home: Build a block graph with blocks or Lego: one block for each person's vote. Talk about how each column is built from equal blocks.

math.u04.choice.04.title: Orange votes
math.u04.choice.04.hint: Find the orange row and count its pictures.
math.u04.choice.04.explanation: The orange row has three pictures, so 3 people chose orange.
math.u04.choice.04.home: In your picture chart, your child counts the pictures in one row and says how many people chose that fruit.

math.u04.choice.05.title: Fair pictograms
math.u04.choice.05.hint: How can we compare the rows fairly?
math.u04.choice.05.explanation: Same-size pictures in lines let us compare rows fairly.
math.u04.choice.05.home: Make two rows of drawings, one spread out and one lined up. Talk about which one is fair to compare.

math.u05.main.01.title: Number words
math.u05.main.01.hint: Say each word aloud, then find its number.
math.u05.main.01.home: Write eleven, fifteen and twenty on cards (in English) and 11, 15 and 20 on other cards. Match them together.

math.u05.main.02.title: Counting back gaps
math.u05.main.02.hint: Count back one at a time: each number is one less.
math.u05.main.02.home: Count backwards from 20 together while walking down the stairs or clapping. Stop and ask your child for the next number.

math.u05.main.03.title: Larger numbers
math.u05.main.03.hint: The larger number comes later when you count.
math.u05.main.03.home: Write pairs of numbers like 14 and 19, or 2 and 20. Your child finds both on a ruler and picks the one further along.

math.u05.main.04.title: Smaller numbers
math.u05.main.04.hint: The smaller number comes first when you count.
math.u05.main.04.home: Build two towers, one of 6 blocks and one of 16. Your child points to the smaller number and the shorter tower.

math.u05.main.05.title: An empty bowl
math.u05.main.05.hint: How many apples can you see in the bowl?
math.u05.main.05.home: Empty the fruit bowl together and ask how many apples are in it now. Write the number 0.

math.u05.main.06.title: Guess, then count
math.u05.main.06.hint: Your guess does not have to match. Touch each dot once.
math.u05.main.06.home: Put some large pasta shapes on a plate. Your child guesses how many, then counts to see how close the guess was.

math.u05.main.07.title: Counting on from 7
math.u05.main.07.hint: Start on 7 and make four jumps forward.

math.u05.main.08.title: Counting back from 15
math.u05.main.08.hint: Start on 15 and make three jumps back.
math.u05.main.08.home: Stand on a tile you call 15 and take 3 steps back, saying 14, 13, 12.

math.u05.choice.01.title: An empty basket
math.u05.choice.01.hint: Look inside the basket. Is anything there?
math.u05.choice.01.explanation: The basket is empty. Zero means nothing at all.
math.u05.choice.01.home: Show an empty basket or bag and ask how many apples are in it. Say together: zero, nothing at all.

math.u05.choice.02.title: The largest number
math.u05.choice.02.hint: Which number would you say last when you count?
math.u05.choice.02.explanation: 17 comes after 9 and 12 when we count, so it is largest.
math.u05.choice.02.home: Write 9, 12 and 17 on cards and put them in order on the table. Your child says which is largest.

math.u05.choice.03.title: Just before 10
math.u05.choice.03.hint: Count up to 10. Which number do you say just before it?
math.u05.choice.03.explanation: 9 comes just before 10 when we count.
math.u05.choice.03.home: Count down for a rocket launch: 10, 9, 8... Stop and ask which number comes just before 10.

math.u05.choice.04.title: A clever guess
math.u05.choice.04.hint: It is a guess we make before we count.
math.u05.choice.04.explanation: An estimate is a clever guess before we count.
math.u05.choice.04.home: Before counting the socks in the laundry, guess the number together and call it an estimate. Then count to check.

math.u05.choice.05.title: Counting back from 12
math.u05.choice.05.hint: Each number is one less than the one before.
math.u05.choice.05.home: Clap and count back from 12 together. Your child says the number after 11.

math.u06.main.01.title: Breakfast time
math.u06.main.01.hint: Think about what you do soon after waking up.
math.u06.main.01.home: At breakfast, talk about the time of day: morning. Name things you do in the morning, the afternoon and the evening.

math.u06.main.02.title: Sleep time
math.u06.main.02.hint: Is it light or dark when you go to bed?
math.u06.main.02.home: Draw a sun and a moon. Your child puts drawings of daily jobs (breakfast, school, sleep) under the right one.

math.u06.main.03.title: A school day
math.u06.main.03.hint: What do you do first when the day starts?
math.u06.main.03.home: Draw three pictures: waking up, going to school, eating dinner. Your child puts them in order and tells the day as a story.

math.u06.main.04.title: Which takes longer
math.u06.main.04.hint: Imagine doing each one. Which lasts all night?
math.u06.main.04.home: Compare brushing your teeth with a night's sleep, from bedtime to waking up. Talk about which takes longer.

math.u06.main.05.title: Which is quicker
math.u06.main.05.hint: Which one is over in a moment?
math.u06.main.05.home: Blink, clap and hum a song. Your child says which one is over the quickest.

math.u06.main.06.title: Comparing ribbons
math.u06.main.06.hint: Check the ribbons start at the same line, then compare the other ends.
math.u06.main.06.home: Lay three ribbons or strings side by side with one end lined up. Your child finds the longest and the shortest.

math.u06.main.07.title: Fair comparing
math.u06.main.07.hint: What happens if one pencil starts further along?
math.u06.main.07.home: Compare two spoons, first with one end lined up and then with the ends apart. Talk about which way is fair.

math.u06.choice.01.title: Moon and stars
math.u06.choice.01.explanation: We see the Moon and stars in the dark night sky.
math.u06.choice.01.home: Look out of the window at night and find the Moon. Talk about when we see the Moon and the stars.

math.u06.choice.02.title: Dinner time
math.u06.choice.02.hint: Is dinner early or late in the day?
math.u06.choice.02.explanation: Dinner is the meal we usually eat in the evening.
math.u06.choice.02.home: At dinner, ask: is it morning, evening or the middle of the night? Look outside to check.

math.u06.choice.03.title: The longest thing
math.u06.choice.03.hint: Which one could you lie down on?
math.u06.choice.03.explanation: A bed is longer than a shoe or a spoon.
math.u06.choice.03.home: Lay a piece of string along a spoon, a shoe and a bed. Your child finds the longest.

math.u06.choice.04.title: Lining up
math.u06.choice.04.explanation: Lining up the ends gives both things the same start.
math.u06.choice.04.home: Stand two pencils with their ends against a book. Your child says which is longer and why the ends must be together.

math.u06.choice.05.title: Opposite of longer
math.u06.choice.05.hint: If one ribbon is longer, the other one is…
math.u06.choice.05.explanation: Shorter is the opposite of longer.
math.u06.choice.05.home: Compare two scarves or ribbons. Say "this one is longer" and your child says the other one "is shorter".

math.q01.01.title: Counting dots
math.q01.01.hint: Touch each dot once and say one number for each.
math.q01.01.home: Draw 9 dots on paper. Your child counts them and crosses out each dot once, so none is counted twice.

math.q01.02.title: One more than 12
math.q01.02.home: Count the steps of the stairs together. Stop on step 12 and ask where one more step takes you.

math.q01.03.title: Take away 3
math.q01.03.hint: Start on 7 and jump back three times.
math.q01.03.home: Put 7 spoons on the table and put 3 back in the drawer. Your child counts how many are left.

math.q01.04.title: Three sides
math.q01.04.hint: Count the straight sides of each shape.
math.q01.04.home: Hunt for triangles at home: a sandwich cut corner to corner, a roof in a drawing. Your child traces the 3 sides with a finger.

math.q01.05.title: Like a football
math.q01.05.hint: Is a football flat or solid? Round or with edges?
math.q01.05.home: Collect a ball, an orange and a tin. Your child finds the ones that are round all over like a football: spheres.

math.q01.06.title: The longest row
math.q01.06.hint: More pictures make a longer row.
math.q01.06.home: Make a spoon chart: one row for each fruit your family likes, and one spoon for each person. The longest row shows the fruit most people chose.

math.q01.07.title: The larger number
math.q01.07.hint: Which number comes later when you count?
math.q01.07.home: Write 15 and 18 on two cards. Your child finds both on a ruler or tape measure and says which is further along, so larger.

math.q01.08.title: An empty bag
math.q01.08.hint: Empty means there is nothing inside.
math.q01.08.home: Show an empty bag or box and ask how many sweets are inside. Practise saying "zero" for nothing at all.

math.q01.09.title: Sleep time
math.q01.09.hint: Is it light or dark when you go to bed?
math.q01.09.home: At bedtime, look out of the window together and talk about why the sky is dark: we sleep at night.

math.q01.10.title: Comparing pencils
math.q01.10.home: Hold two pencils side by side with their ends on the edge of the table. Your child says which is longer, then tries again with the ends not lined up.

math.u07.main.01.title: Both labels
math.u07.main.01.hint: Ask two questions: is it red? Does it have wheels?
math.u07.main.01.home: Make two string hoops on the floor: "red" and "has wheels". Your child puts a red toy car in the overlap.

math.u07.main.02.title: The overlap
math.u07.main.02.hint: Check the car against each label in turn.
math.u07.main.02.home: Ask your child where a red car goes and why: it is red and it has wheels.

math.u07.main.03.title: Neither label
math.u07.main.03.hint: Find the things that are not red and have no wheels.
math.u07.main.03.home: Find things that are not red and have no wheels (a green leaf, a blue ball). Put them outside both hoops.

math.u07.main.04.title: Carroll diagram
math.u07.main.04.hint: For each number ask: is it less than 10? Think about 10 itself.
math.u07.main.04.home: Draw two columns: "less than 10" and "not less than 10". Your child sorts number cards from 1 to 20, thinking hard about 10.

math.u07.main.05.title: Children with cats
math.u07.main.05.hint: Count the blocks in the cat column.
math.u07.main.05.home: Make a block graph of the pets your family and friends have. Your child counts the blocks in the cat column.

math.u07.main.06.title: More cats than dogs
math.u07.main.06.hint: Count both columns, then find the difference.
math.u07.main.06.home: Put the cat and dog towers side by side. Your child counts how many extra blocks the taller tower has.

math.u07.main.07.title: Fitting both labels
math.u07.main.07.hint: Where do the two hoops share space?
math.u07.main.07.home: Play a sorting game with two hoops. Each time something fits both labels, your child puts it in the overlap.

math.u07.choice.01.title: Venn overlap
math.u07.choice.01.hint: The overlap is inside both hoops at once.
math.u07.choice.01.explanation: The overlap is inside both hoops, so things there fit both labels.
math.u07.choice.01.home: Use two hoops, "fruit" and "red". Ask where a red apple goes and why.

math.u07.choice.02.title: Where 10 goes
math.u07.choice.02.hint: Is 10 less than 10, or the same?
math.u07.choice.02.explanation: 10 is the same as 10, so it is not less than 10.
math.u07.choice.02.home: Write 10 on a card and ask: is it less than 10? Talk about why 10 is not less than 10.

math.u07.choice.03.title: Outside the hoops
math.u07.choice.03.hint: If a thing fits no hoop, where can it go?
math.u07.choice.03.explanation: Things that fit neither label go outside both hoops.
math.u07.choice.03.home: With two hoops on the floor, give your child something that fits neither label. Where should it go?

math.u07.choice.04.title: Each block
math.u07.choice.04.hint: Read the words under the graph.
math.u07.choice.04.explanation: Each block in the pets graph stands for one child.
math.u07.choice.04.home: Build a block graph where each block is one child. Your child adds a block for themself.

math.u07.choice.05.title: The tallest column
math.u07.choice.05.hint: More blocks make a taller column.
math.u07.choice.05.explanation: The tallest column has the most blocks, so it is most popular.
math.u07.choice.05.home: Vote on dinner with blocks. The tallest column shows the most popular choice.

math.u08.main.01.title: What comes next
math.u08.main.01.hint: Say the pattern aloud and find the part that repeats.
math.u08.main.01.home: Make a pattern with red and blue plates or cups. Your child says it aloud and puts the next one.

math.u08.main.02.title: Shape pattern
math.u08.main.02.hint: Say the shapes aloud. Which part repeats?
math.u08.main.02.home: An adult cuts paper triangles and circles. Make "triangle, triangle, circle" again and again, and your child continues it.

math.u08.main.03.title: Pattern gaps
math.u08.main.03.hint: Find red, blue, blue, then keep saying it.
math.u08.main.03.home: Clap and stamp a pattern like "clap, stamp, stamp". Stop, and your child does the next two.

math.u08.main.05.title: Steps from the start
math.u08.main.05.hint: Step forward three times, then back once. Where are you now?
math.u08.main.05.home: Walk 3 steps forwards and 1 step back together. Count how many steps from the start you are.

math.u08.main.06.title: Is a cube flat?
math.u08.main.06.hint: Could you hold a cube in your hand?
math.u08.main.06.home: Put a dice next to a paper square. Your child holds each and explains which one is solid.

math.u08.main.07.title: Square and rectangle
math.u08.main.07.hint: Count the sides of each. Are all the sides the same length?
math.u08.main.07.home: Compare a square tile and a book. Count the sides and corners of each, then check which one has all sides equal.

math.u08.main.08.title: Counting corners
math.u08.main.08.hint: Touch and count the corners of each shape.
math.u08.main.08.home: Draw a circle, a triangle, a square and a rectangle. Your child counts the corners of each and groups them.

math.u08.choice.01.title: Colour pattern
math.u08.choice.01.hint: Say the colours aloud. What came after yellow before?
math.u08.choice.01.explanation: Red and yellow take turns, so red comes next.
math.u08.choice.01.home: Line up red and yellow things in turn. Your child says what comes next.

math.u08.choice.02.title: Square sides
math.u08.choice.02.hint: Touch each side of a square and count.
math.u08.choice.02.explanation: A square has four straight sides, all the same length.
math.u08.choice.02.home: Fold a paper napkin into a square. Your child runs a finger along each side and counts: 4.

math.u08.choice.03.title: Moving backwards
math.u08.choice.03.hint: Your face looks forwards. Which way does your back face?
math.u08.choice.03.explanation: Moving the way your back faces is moving backwards.
math.u08.choice.03.home: Play robots: say "forwards", "backwards" or "turn", and your child moves that way.

math.u08.choice.04.title: Turning
math.u08.choice.04.hint: Did it get bigger, change colour, or point a new way?
math.u08.choice.04.explanation: Turning changes the way something points or faces. Its size and colour stay the same.
math.u08.choice.04.home: Point a toy car at the door, then turn it. Talk about what changed: only the way it faces.

math.u08.choice.05.title: 3D shapes
math.u08.choice.05.hint: Think of a ball or a box. Could you pick them up?
math.u08.choice.05.explanation: A 3D shape is solid, so you can pick it up.
math.u08.choice.05.home: Collect solid things from the kitchen (a tin, a box, an orange). Your child holds each and says it is a 3D shape.

math.u09.main.01.title: Ten and ones
math.u09.main.01.hint: Count the full ten, then count on the ones.
math.u09.main.01.home: Bundle 10 straws or pencils and put 4 loose ones beside them. Count on from ten: 11, 12, 13, 14.

math.u09.main.02.title: More tens and ones
math.u09.main.02.hint: Start at 10, then count on each loose one.
math.u09.main.02.home: Show 10 fingers on your hands and 9 on your child's. Count on from ten to find 19.

math.u09.main.03.title: Seventeen
math.u09.main.03.hint: The first digit counts tens; the second counts ones.
math.u09.main.03.home: Make 17 with a bundle of ten pencils and some loose ones. Your child says how many tens and how many ones.

math.u09.main.04.title: Twenty
math.u09.main.04.hint: How many full tens make 20? Are any ones left over?
math.u09.main.04.home: Make two bundles of 10 pencils. Ask how many tens and how many loose ones: 2 tens and no ones.

math.u09.main.05.title: Smallest first
math.u09.main.05.hint: Find the number with no tens first.
math.u09.main.05.home: Write 9, 12, 15 and 20 on cards and mix them up. Your child puts them in order, smallest first.

math.u09.main.06.title: Counting in tens
math.u09.main.06.hint: Each step adds one more ten.
math.u09.main.06.home: Count in tens while jumping: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Leave a gap and let your child fill it.

math.u09.main.07.title: Tens from 4
math.u09.main.07.hint: Add a ten each time. The ones digit stays the same.
math.u09.main.07.home: Start at 4 on a tape measure and jump in tens: 4, 14, 24, 34.

math.u09.main.08.title: Writing sixteen
math.u09.main.08.hint: Sixteen is one ten and six ones. Which digit comes first?
math.u09.main.08.home: Write 16 and 61 on cards. Make 16 with a bundle of ten and 6 loose pencils, and see which card it matches.

math.u09.choice.01.title: Tens in 13
math.u09.choice.01.hint: How many full tens fit in 13? How many are left?
math.u09.choice.01.explanation: 13 is one full ten and three more ones.
math.u09.choice.01.home: Make 13 with a bundle of ten and 3 loose pencils. Your child says: one ten and three ones.

math.u09.choice.02.title: Ten more
math.u09.choice.02.explanation: Ten more than 5 is one ten and five ones: 15.
math.u09.choice.02.home: Put down 5 loose pencils and add a bundle of ten. Count on to find ten more than 5.

math.u09.choice.03.title: Tens pattern
math.u09.choice.03.hint: Each number is ten more than the one before.
math.u09.choice.03.home: Count everyone's fingers around the table in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40.

math.u09.choice.04.title: In order
math.u09.choice.04.hint: Check that each number is bigger than the one before.
math.u09.choice.04.explanation: 4, then 11, then 18: each number is bigger than the last.
math.u09.choice.04.home: Write 4, 11 and 18 on cards. Your child lays them on a tape measure in order and reads them smallest first.

math.u09.choice.05.title: The 1 in 18
math.u09.choice.05.hint: In 18, the first digit counts tens.
math.u09.choice.05.explanation: The 1 in 18 stands for one whole ten, the full ten frame.
math.u09.choice.05.home: Make 18 with a bundle of ten and 8 loose pencils. Point to the 1 in 18 and to the bundle: both mean one ten.

math.u10.main.01.title: Days in a week
math.u10.main.01.hint: Say the days from Sunday to Saturday and count them.
math.u10.main.01.home: Sing or say the days of the week together, holding up one finger for each day.

math.u10.main.02.title: Neighbouring days
math.u10.main.02.hint: Say the days in order. Which comes after Monday?
math.u10.main.02.home: Write the days of the week on cards in a circle. Your child finds the day before and the day after a day you choose.

math.u10.main.03.title: Months in a year
math.u10.main.03.hint: Say the months from January to December and count them.
math.u10.main.03.home: Look at a calendar and count the months together. Find the month of your child's birthday.

math.u10.main.04.title: After January
math.u10.main.04.hint: Say the months in order, starting from January.
math.u10.main.04.home: Say the months in order together. Stop at a month and ask which one comes next.

math.u10.main.05.title: Measuring with cubes
math.u10.main.05.hint: Count the cubes from one end of the pencil to the other.
math.u10.main.05.home: Measure a pencil or a spoon with blocks laid end to end, with no gaps. Count the blocks.

math.u10.main.06.title: The heavier side
math.u10.main.06.hint: Which side of the balance went down?
math.u10.main.06.home: Hold something heavy in one hand and something light in the other, like a balance. Your child lowers the hand holding the heavier one.

math.u10.main.07.title: Big and heavy
math.u10.main.07.hint: Think of a big pillow and a small stone.
math.u10.main.07.home: Hold a big pillow in one hand and a small stone in the other. Talk about which is bigger and which is heavier.

math.u10.main.08.title: Heaviest first
math.u10.main.08.hint: Imagine lifting each one. Which is hardest to lift?
math.u10.main.08.home: With an adult's help, compare lifting a chair, a book and a tissue. Put them in order from heaviest to lightest.

math.u10.choice.01.title: A year
math.u10.choice.01.hint: Say the months from January to December.
math.u10.choice.01.explanation: A year has 12 months, from January to December.
math.u10.choice.01.home: Turn the pages of a calendar and count one page for each month: 12.

math.u10.choice.02.title: Balance rule
math.u10.choice.02.hint: Look at the balance. Which pan is lower?
math.u10.choice.02.explanation: The heavier side pulls its pan down.
math.u10.choice.02.home: Hang two bags on a coat hanger. Put a full can in one and an empty cup in the other, and watch which side goes down.

math.u10.choice.03.title: Measuring fairly
math.u10.choice.03.hint: Would gaps change how many cubes you count?
math.u10.choice.03.explanation: Cubes must touch, with no gaps, to measure the whole length.
math.u10.choice.03.home: Measure a book with blocks twice: once with gaps between them and once with none. Talk about which count is right.

math.u10.choice.04.title: After Saturday
math.u10.choice.04.hint: What happens to the week after Saturday?
math.u10.choice.04.explanation: After Saturday the week starts again with Sunday.
math.u10.choice.04.home: Lay the days of the week in a circle on the floor. Walk round it and find what comes after Saturday.

math.u10.choice.05.title: The heaviest
math.u10.choice.05.hint: Which one would be hardest to carry?
math.u10.choice.05.explanation: A watermelon is much heavier than a grape or a strawberry.
math.u10.choice.05.home: At the market or at home, hold a grape, a strawberry and a watermelon (with help). Talk about which is heaviest.

math.u11.main.01.title: Partners of 10
math.u11.main.01.hint: Use a ten frame: how many spaces are still empty?
math.u11.main.01.home: Hold up 10 fingers and fold some down. Your child says how many are up and how many are down: together they always make 10.

math.u11.main.02.title: Empty spaces
math.u11.main.02.hint: Fill 7 spaces, then count the empty ones.
math.u11.main.02.home: Draw a ten frame and fill 7 boxes. Your child counts the empty boxes needed to make 10.

math.u11.main.03.title: The same total
math.u11.main.03.hint: Count on from the bigger number in each sum.
math.u11.main.03.home: Make 5 in different ways with blocks of two colours: 3 and 2, 4 and 1. Count each total.

math.u11.main.04.title: Adding on a line
math.u11.main.04.hint: Start on 12 and make three jumps forward.
math.u11.main.04.home: On a tape measure, start at 12 and make 3 jumps forward with a finger.

math.u11.main.05.title: Taking away 4
math.u11.main.05.hint: Count 16 cubes, cover 4, then count the cubes left.
math.u11.main.05.home: Make a line of 16 blocks, take 4 away and count what is left.

math.u11.main.06.title: Difference of 5 and 9
math.u11.main.06.hint: Start on 5 and count the jumps to 9.
math.u11.main.06.home: Build towers of 5 and 9 blocks side by side. Your child counts the extra blocks on the taller one.

math.u11.main.07.title: A sensible total
math.u11.main.07.hint: Is 6 + 3 small or big? Could it be near 20?
math.u11.main.07.home: Ask: can 6 and 3 make 19? Check on fingers: 6 on one hand and 3 on the other make 9.

math.u11.main.08.title: Hidden beans
math.u11.main.08.home: Hide some of 10 spoons under a towel and show the rest. Your child works out how many are hiding.

math.u11.choice.01.title: Making 10
math.u11.choice.01.hint: Check each pair on a ten frame.
math.u11.choice.01.explanation: 6 and 4 fill all ten spaces of a ten frame.
math.u11.choice.01.home: Play "make 10" with fingers: you show 6, and your child shows the number that makes 10.

math.u11.choice.02.title: Difference of 8 and 10
math.u11.choice.02.hint: Start on 8 and count the jumps to 10.
math.u11.choice.02.explanation: Two jumps go from 8 to 10, so the difference is 2.
math.u11.choice.02.home: Count from 8 to 10 on your fingers: how many jumps is it?

math.u11.choice.03.title: Adding 2 to 14
math.u11.choice.03.hint: Start on 14 and jump forward twice.
math.u11.choice.03.explanation: Two jumps forward from 14 land on 16.
math.u11.choice.03.home: Say 14 and count on 2 more steps on the stairs.

math.u11.choice.04.title: Adding 1 to 9
math.u11.choice.04.home: Fill a ten frame with 9 and add one more. Talk about how one more than 9 makes 10.

math.u11.choice.05.title: Taking 3 from 18
math.u11.choice.05.hint: Start on 18 and jump back three times.
math.u11.choice.05.explanation: Three jumps back from 18 land on 15.
math.u11.choice.05.home: Start at 18 on a tape measure and make 3 jumps back.

math.u12.main.01.title: Equal parts
math.u12.main.01.hint: Look at each cut. Are both parts the same size?
math.u12.main.01.home: Fold paper shapes in half and an adult cuts along the fold. Put the two parts on top of each other: do they match?

math.u12.main.02.title: Half of 6
math.u12.main.02.hint: Share 6 into two groups, one at a time.
math.u12.main.02.home: Share 6 biscuits between two plates, one at a time. Count each plate.

math.u12.main.03.title: Half of 10
math.u12.main.03.hint: Share 10 into two groups, one at a time.
math.u12.main.03.home: Share 10 spoons between two people, one each in turn. Each person counts their share.

math.u12.main.04.title: Sharing apples
math.u12.main.04.hint: Give one apple to each child in turn.
math.u12.main.04.home: Share 8 pieces of fruit between two children, one at a time, and check that both have the same.

math.u12.main.05.title: What a half is
math.u12.main.05.hint: When we halve, how many equal parts are there?
math.u12.main.05.home: Fold a sheet of paper into two equal parts. Colour one part and call it one half.

math.u12.main.06.title: The bigger half
math.u12.main.06.hint: Can two halves of the same thing be different sizes?
math.u12.main.06.home: An adult cuts a sandwich in two. If one part is bigger, talk about why the parts are not halves.

math.u12.choice.01.title: Fair halves
math.u12.choice.01.hint: Halves are two parts of the same size.
math.u12.choice.01.explanation: Picture c has two equal parts, so they are halves. The others are not.
math.u12.choice.01.home: Draw lines on some shapes, some through the middle and some not. Your child picks the shapes cut into two equal halves.

math.u12.choice.02.title: Half of 4
math.u12.choice.02.explanation: Two and two make 4, so half of 4 is 2.
math.u12.choice.02.home: Share 4 spoons between two cups. Your child counts how many are in each cup.

math.u12.choice.03.title: Pizza halves
math.u12.choice.03.hint: The pizza has two equal parts. What is one of them called?
math.u12.choice.03.explanation: One of two equal parts is one half.
math.u12.choice.03.home: When an adult cuts a pizza or a round loaf into two equal parts, ask your child to name each part: one half.

math.u12.choice.04.title: Sharing 6
math.u12.choice.04.hint: Give one to each person in turn until none are left.
math.u12.choice.04.explanation: Sharing 6 fairly between 2 people gives 3 each.
math.u12.choice.04.home: Share 6 toys between two people, one each in turn, and count each share.

math.u12.choice.05.title: Cut into equal parts
math.u12.choice.05.hint: Are all the pieces the same size?
math.u12.choice.05.explanation: The square is cut into four equal parts. Equal parts of a whole are a fraction.
math.u12.choice.05.home: Fold a paper square into 4 equal parts and open it. Your child checks that all the parts are the same size.

math.q02.01.title: Venn overlap
math.q02.01.hint: The overlap is inside both hoops.
math.q02.01.home: Make two hoops with string on the floor: "red" and "toys". A red toy goes in the overlap, because it fits both.

math.q02.02.title: Colour pattern
math.q02.02.hint: Say the colours aloud and find the part that repeats.
math.q02.02.home: Make a red, blue, red, blue line with cups or blocks. Your child says the pattern aloud and adds the next one.

math.q02.03.title: Tens and ones in 15
math.q02.03.hint: The first digit counts tens; the second counts ones.
math.q02.03.home: Bundle 10 pencils with a rubber band and put 5 loose ones beside them. Your child says: one ten and five ones make 15.

math.q02.04.title: Counting in tens
math.q02.04.home: Each family member holds up 10 fingers. Count the hands in tens: ten, twenty, thirty.

math.q02.05.title: Every day for a week
math.q02.05.hint: Say the days from Sunday to Saturday and count them.
math.q02.05.home: Mark each day on a calendar for one week. Count the marks together: seven days, from Sunday to Saturday.

math.q02.06.title: Balance rule
math.q02.06.hint: Look at the balance. Which pan is lower?
math.q02.06.home: Make a balance with a coat hanger and two bags. Put something heavy in one bag and something light in the other, and watch which side goes down.

math.q02.07.title: Partner of 8
math.q02.07.hint: Fill 8 spaces of a ten frame. How many are empty?
math.q02.07.home: Draw a ten frame (2 rows of 5 boxes) and put a dot in 8 boxes. Your child counts the empty boxes: the partner of 8 that makes 10.

math.q02.08.title: Difference of 7 and 10
math.q02.08.hint: Start on 7 and count the jumps to 10.
math.q02.08.home: Draw a number line on paper. Your child puts a finger on 7 and counts the jumps to 10.

math.q02.09.title: Half of 8
math.q02.09.home: Share 8 biscuits fairly between two plates, one at a time. Count how many are on each plate.

math.q02.10.title: Equal halves
math.q02.10.hint: Can halves of the same whole be different sizes?
math.q02.10.home: An adult cuts a slice of bread into a big piece and a small piece. Ask: are these halves? Then cut another slice into two equal halves and compare.

math.u13.main.01.title: Even numbers
math.u13.main.01.hint: Can each number make pairs with none left over?
math.u13.main.01.home: Pair up socks or shoes for numbers like 2, 5, 8 and 11. Your child sorts the numbers into "none left over" and "one left over".

math.u13.main.02.title: Odd or even
math.u13.main.02.hint: Pair up 7 things. Is one left alone?
math.u13.main.02.home: Put out 7 socks and make pairs. Your child finds the sock left alone, so 7 is odd.

math.u13.main.03.title: Counting in twos
math.u13.main.03.hint: Each number is two more than the one before.
math.u13.main.03.home: Count the shoes by the door in twos: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

math.u13.main.04.title: Race positions
math.u13.main.04.hint: Who finished just after the one who came 1st?
math.u13.main.04.home: Have a short race with toys or family members. Say who came 1st, 2nd and 3rd.

math.u13.main.05.title: Third from the left
math.u13.main.05.hint: Touch the stars from the left: first, second, third.
math.u13.main.05.home: Line up 5 toys. Your child points to the 1st, the 2nd and the 3rd from the left.

math.u13.main.06.title: Parts of 14
math.u13.main.06.hint: What do you add to 10 to make 14? And to 7?
math.u13.main.06.home: Make 14 with blocks and split it in different ways: 10 and 4, 7 and 7. Count each part.

math.u13.main.07.title: Coin values
math.u13.main.07.hint: Read the value on each coin, not its size.
math.u13.main.07.home: Look at real coins together (25 and 50 piastres and 1 pound). Read the number on each and find the one worth most.

math.u13.main.08.title: Pairs of socks
math.u13.main.08.hint: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in twos.
math.u13.main.08.home: Put 5 pairs of socks on the bed and count every sock in twos.

math.u13.choice.01.title: Pairs with none left
math.u13.choice.01.hint: Make pairs of socks. Is one left alone?
math.u13.choice.01.explanation: 6 socks make 3 pairs with none left over, so 6 is even.
math.u13.choice.01.home: Pair up 6 socks from the laundry. Your child checks whether any sock is left alone.

math.u13.choice.02.title: An odd number
math.u13.choice.02.hint: Pair up each number. Which one leaves one alone?
math.u13.choice.02.explanation: 9 makes four pairs with one left over, so it is odd.
math.u13.choice.02.home: Try pairing 9, 12 and 4 spoons. Your child finds the number that leaves one spoon alone.

math.u13.choice.03.title: After 2nd
math.u13.choice.03.hint: Say first, second, then the next position.
math.u13.choice.03.home: Queue toys in a line for a bus. Ask who is 2nd and who comes after them.

math.u13.choice.04.title: Egyptian money
math.u13.choice.04.hint: What are the coins and notes in Egypt called?
math.u13.choice.04.explanation: In Egypt we pay with pounds and piastres.
math.u13.choice.04.home: Look at coins and a note together and talk about pounds and piastres. Let your child hand over the money when you buy something small.

math.u13.choice.05.title: Making 12
math.u13.choice.05.hint: Start at 10. How many more make 12?
math.u13.choice.05.explanation: Ten and two more make twelve.
math.u13.choice.05.home: Make 12 with a bundle of ten pencils and 2 loose ones. Your child says: 12 is 10 and 2.

math.u14.main.01.title: Doubles
math.u14.main.01.hint: A double is the same number added again.
math.u14.main.01.home: Use a mirror: put 2 blocks in front of it and count what you see. Try 5 too.

math.u14.main.02.title: Bigger doubles
math.u14.main.02.home: Count fingers in doubles: two hands of 5 make 10. Use blocks for double 7 and double 10.

math.u14.main.03.title: Counting on from 8
math.u14.main.03.hint: Start on 8, the bigger number, and count on 3.
math.u14.main.03.home: Say 8 and count on 3 fingers. Then start at 3 instead, and talk about which was quicker.

math.u14.main.04.title: Counting on from 12
math.u14.main.04.hint: Start on 12, the bigger number, and count on 5.
math.u14.main.04.home: Say 12 and count on 5 steps across the room.

math.u14.main.05.title: More birds
math.u14.main.05.hint: Start on 8 and count on 4 more.
math.u14.main.05.home: Tell a story with toys: 8 toys are at a party and 4 more arrive. Count them all.

math.u14.main.06.title: Counting back from 15
math.u14.main.06.hint: Start on 15 and jump back three times.
math.u14.main.06.home: Start at 15 and count back 3 claps: 14, 13, 12.

math.u14.main.07.title: Difference of 13 and 17
math.u14.main.07.hint: Start on 13 and count the jumps to 17.
math.u14.main.07.home: On a tape measure, put one finger on 13 and another on 17. Count the jumps between them.

math.u14.choice.01.title: Double 6
math.u14.choice.01.home: Put 6 blocks on each of two plates. Count them all: double 6.

math.u14.choice.02.title: The quickest start
math.u14.choice.02.explanation: Starting on the bigger number, 9, needs only two jumps.
math.u14.choice.02.home: Ask: for 2 + 9, would you start counting from 2 or from 9? Try both on your fingers.

math.u14.choice.03.title: Swapping numbers
math.u14.choice.03.hint: Does the order of adding change the total?
math.u14.choice.03.explanation: Swapping the numbers does not change the total: 3 + 7 is 10 too.
math.u14.choice.03.home: Line up 7 red and 3 blue blocks, then turn the line round. Count both ways: still 10.

math.u14.choice.04.title: Taking 2 from 20
math.u14.choice.04.hint: Start on 20 and jump back twice.
math.u14.choice.04.explanation: Two jumps back from 20 land on 18.
math.u14.choice.04.home: Start at 20 on the stairs or a tape measure and go back 2.

math.u14.choice.05.title: Double 8
math.u14.choice.05.home: Build two towers of 8 blocks. Count them together: double 8.

math.u15.main.01.title: Cube faces
math.u15.main.01.hint: Count each flat face of a dice once.
math.u15.main.01.home: Hold a dice or a cube-shaped box. Put a sticker on each face as you count: 6 faces.

math.u15.main.02.title: Cube corners
math.u15.main.02.hint: Count the top corners, then the bottom corners.
math.u15.main.02.home: Count the corners of a cube-shaped box, touching each one once: 4 on top and 4 underneath.

math.u15.main.03.title: Turned shapes
math.u15.main.03.hint: Count the sides of each. Did turning change them?
math.u15.main.03.home: Turn a box on its side and on its end. Ask each time: is it still the same shape?

math.u15.main.04.title: Cylinder faces
math.u15.main.04.hint: Look at a tin: how many flat ends does it have?
math.u15.main.04.home: Hold a tin and find its flat faces, top and bottom. Feel the curved side in between.

math.u15.main.05.title: Solid pattern
math.u15.main.05.hint: Say the shapes aloud and find the part that repeats.
math.u15.main.05.home: Make a pattern with balls and boxes: ball, box, box, ball, box, box. Your child says what comes next.

math.u15.main.07.title: Flat or curved faces
math.u15.main.07.hint: Does the shape have a curved surface that can roll?
math.u15.main.07.home: Collect a ball, a tin, a box and a party hat. Sort them: has a curved face, or only flat faces.

math.u15.main.08.title: Robot routes
math.u15.main.08.hint: Choose a route and watch where the robot ends.
math.u15.main.08.home: Make a grid on the floor with chalk or tape. Your child gives you robot commands (forwards, turn right) to reach a toy.

math.u15.choice.01.title: Turning a shape
math.u15.choice.01.hint: Turn a triangle. Does it still have 3 sides?
math.u15.choice.01.explanation: Turning does not change sides or corners, so the name stays.
math.u15.choice.01.home: Turn a paper triangle in different ways. Each time, ask your child to name it.

math.u15.choice.02.title: Cone corners
math.u15.choice.02.hint: Where does a cone come to a point?
math.u15.choice.02.explanation: A cone has one pointy corner at its top.
math.u15.choice.02.home: Look at an ice cream cone or a party hat. Find its one pointy corner and its round flat face.

math.u15.choice.03.title: Sphere faces
math.u15.choice.03.explanation: A sphere has one curved face all the way round.
math.u15.choice.03.home: Roll an orange between your hands. Talk about how a sphere has one curved face and no corners.

math.u15.choice.04.title: Cuboid faces
math.u15.choice.04.hint: Count the faces of a box: top, bottom and the sides.
math.u15.choice.04.explanation: A box shape has a top, a bottom and four sides: 6 faces.
math.u15.choice.04.home: Count the faces of a tissue box, putting a hand on each one: 6.

math.u15.choice.05.title: Triangle sides
math.u15.choice.05.hint: Touch each straight side of a triangle.
math.u15.choice.05.explanation: A triangle has three straight sides.
math.u15.choice.05.home: Make a triangle with three spoons. Count the sides.

math.u16.main.01.title: Children who walked
math.u16.main.01.hint: Find the walk column and count its blocks.
math.u16.main.01.home: Ask relatives or friends how they travel to school or work and make a block graph. Count the "walk" column.

math.u16.main.02.title: The bus column
math.u16.main.02.hint: Find the bus column and count its blocks.
math.u16.main.02.home: In your block graph, count the bus column and write the number under it.

math.u16.main.03.title: Most popular
math.u16.main.03.home: Your child finds the tallest column in your graph and says which way was most popular.

math.u16.main.04.title: Least popular
math.u16.main.04.home: Find the shortest column and say which way was least popular.

math.u16.main.05.title: Walk or car
math.u16.main.05.hint: Count both columns, then find the difference.
math.u16.main.05.home: Put two towers side by side and count how many more blocks the taller one has.

math.u16.main.06.title: Everyone in the graph
math.u16.main.06.hint: Add the blocks in every column.
math.u16.main.06.home: Count every block in your graph to find how many people you asked altogether.

math.u16.main.07.title: Corners or none
math.u16.main.07.hint: Run your finger round each shape. Does it turn a corner?
math.u16.main.07.home: Draw round a cup, a book, half a sandwich and an egg. Sort the drawings: has corners, or no corners.

math.u16.choice.01.title: The tallest column
math.u16.choice.01.hint: More blocks make a taller column.
math.u16.choice.01.explanation: The tallest column has the most blocks.
math.u16.choice.01.home: Your child builds the tallest tower for the family's favourite game. Talk about why it is the tallest.

math.u16.choice.02.title: The car column
math.u16.choice.02.hint: Find the car column and count its blocks.
math.u16.choice.02.explanation: The car column has three blocks: 3 children.
math.u16.choice.02.home: Count the car column in your graph, touching each block once.

math.u16.choice.03.title: Bus and bike
math.u16.choice.03.hint: Count the bus blocks, then count on the bike blocks.
math.u16.choice.03.explanation: Four bus blocks and two bike blocks make six.
math.u16.choice.03.home: Count two columns of your graph together and say the total.

math.u16.choice.04.title: Graph titles
math.u16.choice.04.hint: How do we know what a graph is about?
math.u16.choice.04.explanation: The title tells us what the graph is about.
math.u16.choice.04.home: Make a graph together and let your child write or draw its title at the top.

math.u16.choice.05.title: An empty column
math.u16.choice.05.hint: How many blocks are in the fish column?
math.u16.choice.05.explanation: The fish column has no blocks, so zero children chose fish.
math.u16.choice.05.home: Add a column to your graph that nobody chose. Your child says how many blocks it has: zero.

math.u17.main.01.title: Writing a half
math.u17.main.01.hint: A half is 1 part out of 2.
math.u17.main.01.home: Fold a sheet of paper in half, colour one part and write ½ on it together.

math.u17.main.02.title: Half of 20
math.u17.main.02.home: Share 20 blocks into two equal rows. Count one row.

math.u17.main.03.title: Half of 14
math.u17.main.03.home: Share 14 spoons between two cups, one at a time, and count each cup.

math.u17.main.04.title: Half of 12
math.u17.main.04.home: Make two equal rows from 12 toys and count one row.

math.u17.main.05.title: Half coloured
math.u17.main.05.hint: Is the coloured part one of two equal parts?
math.u17.main.05.home: Fold some shapes in half and colour one part; fold others into unequal parts. Your child picks the ones with one half coloured.

math.u17.main.06.title: Two halves
math.u17.main.06.hint: Put two halves of a pizza back together.
math.u17.main.06.home: An adult cuts an apple in half. Put the halves back together: one whole apple.

math.u17.main.07.title: Half a team
math.u17.main.07.hint: If one half is 5, what is the other half?
math.u17.main.07.home: Line up 5 toys as half a team. Your child makes the other half and counts the whole team.

math.u17.choice.01.title: Showing ½
math.u17.choice.01.hint: Do the two parts have to be the same size?
math.u17.choice.01.explanation: ½ is one of two equal parts, as in picture a.
math.u17.choice.01.home: Draw shapes cut into 2 equal parts and into 2 unequal parts. Your child colours ½ only where the parts are equal.

math.u17.choice.02.title: Half of 16
math.u17.choice.02.explanation: Eight and eight make 16, so half of 16 is 8.
math.u17.choice.02.home: Share 16 pencils between two people, one each in turn, and count each share.

math.u17.choice.03.title: Halves together
math.u17.choice.03.hint: Put the two halves back together.
math.u17.choice.03.explanation: Two halves together make one whole.
math.u17.choice.03.home: Put the two halves of a paper circle together and talk about the whole circle they make.

math.u17.choice.04.title: Half of 18
math.u17.choice.04.explanation: Nine and nine make 18, so half of 18 is 9.
math.u17.choice.04.home: Make 18 with blocks in two equal rows. Count one row.

math.u17.choice.05.title: Middle of a string
math.u17.choice.05.hint: How could you make both parts exactly the same?
math.u17.choice.05.explanation: Folding the ends together finds the middle exactly.
math.u17.choice.05.home: Take a piece of string or ribbon, hold the two ends together and find the fold: that is the middle.

math.u18.main.01.title: O'clock
math.u18.main.01.hint: Look at the long hand first, then the short hand.
math.u18.main.01.home: Set a toy or paper clock to 4 o'clock. Your child says where the long hand and the short hand point.

math.u18.main.02.title: Half past
math.u18.main.02.hint: The long hand on 6 means half past. Where is the short hand?
math.u18.main.02.home: At half past seven, look at a clock together: the long hand points to 6 and the short hand is between 7 and 8.

math.u18.main.04.title: Clock hands
math.u18.main.04.hint: Which hand moves quickly around the clock?
math.u18.main.04.home: Point to the two hands of a clock and name them: the long minute hand and the short hour hand.

math.u18.main.05.title: Measuring tools
math.u18.main.05.hint: What do we measure: length, weight or water?
math.u18.main.05.home: In the kitchen, match tools to jobs: scales to weigh flour, a jug for water, a ruler for a pencil.

math.u18.main.06.title: Holds the most
math.u18.main.06.hint: Compare how many cups each one holds.
math.u18.main.06.home: At the sink, fill a mug with water and pour it into a bowl and a jug. Count how many mugs each one holds.

math.u18.main.08.title: The long hand at half past
math.u18.main.08.hint: Halfway around the clock, where is the long hand?
math.u18.main.08.home: Move the hands of a toy clock to half past. Your child shows that the long hand points to 6.

math.u18.choice.01.title: 3 o'clock
math.u18.choice.01.hint: At any o'clock, where is the long hand?
math.u18.choice.01.explanation: At o'clock the long hand always points to 12.
math.u18.choice.01.home: At 3 o'clock, look at a clock and check where the long hand points: 12.

math.u18.choice.02.title: Half past 5
math.u18.choice.02.hint: After half an hour, has the short hand reached 6 yet?
math.u18.choice.02.explanation: At half past 5 the short hand is halfway to 6.
math.u18.choice.02.home: Set a toy clock to half past 5. Talk about why the short hand is between 5 and 6.

math.u18.choice.03.title: Weighing
math.u18.choice.03.hint: Which tool shows how heavy something is?
math.u18.choice.03.explanation: Scales show how heavy a parcel is.
math.u18.choice.03.home: Weigh a small parcel or a bag of fruit on the kitchen scales together.

math.u18.choice.04.title: Capacity
math.u18.choice.04.hint: What word means how much a container holds?
math.u18.choice.04.explanation: Capacity means how much a container can hold.
math.u18.choice.04.home: At the sink, pour water from a jug into cups. Talk about which container holds more: it has the bigger capacity.

math.u18.choice.05.title: Half an hour
math.u18.choice.05.hint: One hour is 60 minutes. What is half of 60?
math.u18.choice.05.explanation: An hour is 60 minutes, so half an hour is 30.
math.u18.choice.05.home: Set a timer for 30 minutes of play. Tell your child that half an hour is 30 minutes.

math.q03.01.title: An even number
math.q03.01.hint: Which number makes pairs with none left over?
math.q03.01.home: Pair up 6 socks, then try 3 and 9. Your child says which numbers pair up with none left over.

math.q03.02.title: After 2nd
math.q03.02.hint: Say first, second, then the next position.
math.q03.02.home: Line up three toys for a race. Your child gives them places, 1st, 2nd and 3rd, and says who comes after 2nd.

math.q03.03.title: Double 4
math.q03.03.home: Hold up 4 fingers on each hand. Your child counts all the fingers: double 4 is 8.

math.q03.04.title: Adding 6 and 11
math.q03.04.hint: Start on 11, the bigger number, and count on 6.
math.q03.04.home: Say 11 and keep it in your head, then count on 6 fingers: 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17.

math.q03.05.title: Faces of a dice
math.q03.05.hint: Count each flat face of a dice once.
math.q03.05.home: Hold a dice or a small box. Your child touches each flat face once while you count: six faces.

math.q03.06.title: An upside-down triangle
math.q03.06.hint: Count its sides and corners after turning.
math.q03.06.home: An adult cuts a triangle from paper. Turn it round and upside down, and each time count its 3 sides and 3 corners: it is still a triangle.

math.q03.07.title: The most in a graph
math.q03.07.hint: More blocks make a taller column.
math.q03.07.home: Build a tower of blocks or cups for each person's favourite fruit. The tallest tower shows the most popular one.

math.q03.08.title: Sharing 20 fairly
math.q03.08.home: Share 20 spoons or pencils between two people, one each in turn. Count each share: 10 and 10.

math.q03.09.title: Reading the clock
math.q03.09.hint: Look at the long hand first, then the short hand.
math.q03.09.home: Look at a clock together at 2 o'clock. Point to the long hand on 12 and the short hand on 2.

math.q03.10.title: Weighing flour
math.q03.10.hint: Which tool shows how heavy something is?
math.q03.10.home: In the kitchen, weigh a bag of flour or rice on the scales together. Talk about why a ruler or a jug would not work.

math.charts.01.title: Counting cars
math.charts.01.hint: Find the cars column and count its blocks.
math.charts.01.home: Put 4 toy cars in a box with a few other toys. Your child counts only the cars, touching each one once.

math.charts.02.title: The most toys
math.charts.02.home: Make three short rows of toys (for example 4 cars, 2 balls and 3 dolls). Ask which row is longest and which toy there is most of.

math.charts.03.title: All the toys
math.charts.03.hint: Add the blocks in every column.
math.charts.03.home: Sort 10 toys into small groups by kind. Your child counts each group, then all of them together, to find the total.

math.charts.04.title: The best day
math.charts.04.hint: Which day's row has the most stars?
math.charts.04.home: For one week, draw a star on each day your child helps at home. At the end, find the day with the most stars.

math.charts.05.title: Two days together
math.charts.05.hint: Count Monday's stars, then count on Tuesday's.
math.charts.05.home: Draw 3 stars for Monday and 1 for Tuesday. Your child counts both days together and says the total.

math.charts.06.title: How many more stars
math.charts.06.hint: Count both rows, then find the difference.
math.charts.06.home: Line up 4 spoons for Wednesday and 2 for Sunday, side by side. Your child finds how many more are in the longer line.

math.charts.07.title: Sparrows
math.charts.07.hint: Follow the top of the sparrows bar across to the numbers.
math.charts.07.home: Watch the birds from a window or balcony and draw one line for each bird you see. Count the lines for one kind of bird.

math.charts.08.title: The fewest birds
math.charts.08.home: Draw a simple bar for each kind of bird you saw. Your child points to the shortest bar and says which bird it is.

math.charts.09.title: Pigeons and crows
math.charts.09.hint: Read both bars, then add them.
math.charts.09.home: Lay out 6 pencils for pigeons and 3 for crows. Your child adds the two groups, then counts them all to check.

math.u01.main.05.title: Count the circles
math.u01.main.05.hint: Touch each circle once. The last number you say is how many.
math.u01.main.05.home: Draw 9 circles on paper together. Your child counts them, touching each one once, and checks there are not 10.

math.u01.main.08.title: Toy cars in a room
math.u01.main.08.hint: Count each car once, even when the cars are spread out.
math.u01.main.08.home: Count something real in your child's room together, such as toy cars or books. Ask: what did you count, and how many?

math.u03.main.08.title: Triangles in a house
math.u03.main.08.hint: Look at the roof and the flags. Count every shape with three sides.
math.u03.main.08.home: Draw a house together using squares, rectangles and triangles. Count the triangles together.

math.u04.main.08.title: Colour votes
math.u04.main.08.hint: Each circle is one vote. Count all the circles.
math.u04.main.08.home: Ask 4 family members their favourite colour. Your child draws one circle of the same size for each vote.

math.u06.main.08.title: Afternoon time
math.u06.main.08.hint: Afternoon comes after lunch. Breakfast is in the morning.
math.u06.main.08.home: Your child draws something they do in the afternoon and tells you about it.

math.u07.main.08.title: Not red, no wheels
math.u07.main.08.hint: Ask two questions: is it red? Does it have wheels? Two no answers mean outside.
math.u07.main.08.home: Find something at home that is not red and has no wheels. Ask your child why it fits neither label.

math.u08.main.04.title: A pattern that repeats
math.u08.main.04.hint: Find the part that repeats. Does it come again and again?
math.u08.main.04.home: Make a repeating pattern with two kinds of objects, such as spoons and cups. Repeat the part at least twice.

math.u12.main.07.title: One fair cut
math.u12.main.07.hint: Equal parts are the same size. Look for the line through the middle.
math.u12.main.07.home: Draw a rectangle on paper. Your child draws one line that cuts it into two equal parts and checks both parts.

math.u12.main.08.title: A fair share
math.u12.main.08.hint: Half for each friend: both groups must have the same number.
math.u12.main.08.home: Share a snack in half with your child, such as an orange or a pack of biscuits. Check that both parts are equal.

math.u14.main.08.title: A story for 6 + 4
math.u14.main.08.hint: Adding joins two groups. Which story ends with more?
math.u14.main.08.home: Make up a story for 6 + 4 = 10 together and act it out with small toys.

math.u15.main.06.title: Circle hunt
math.u15.main.06.hint: A circle is round and has no corners.
math.u15.main.06.home: At the playground, look for circle shapes together: a wheel, a swing seat, the top of a bin.

math.u16.main.08.title: A question for the graph
math.u16.main.08.hint: The graph shows how the children came to school.
math.u16.main.08.home: Look at a graph together. Your child asks you a question about it, and you both use the graph to check the answer.

math.u17.main.08.title: Cake halves
math.u17.main.08.hint: Two halves are the same size.
math.u17.main.08.home: Draw a cake together. Your child draws one line that divides it into two equal halves.

math.u18.main.03.title: Nine o'clock
math.u18.main.03.hint: At o'clock, the long hand points to 12.
math.u18.main.03.home: Draw a clock on paper. Your child draws the hands for 9 o'clock: long hand on 12, short hand on 9.

math.u18.main.07.title: Lunchtime
math.u18.main.07.hint: Half past: the long hand points to 6.
math.u18.main.07.home: Ask your child what time lunch is. Show it on a paper clock and check the hands together.

math.u02.sheet.01.title: Jump forward
math.u02.sheet.01.hint: Start on the dot. Make 3 jumps forward, one number at a time.
math.u02.sheet.01.home: Draw a number line from 0 to 10. Your child puts a toy on 4 and hops it forward 3.

math.u02.sheet.02.title: Jump back
math.u02.sheet.02.home: On the number line, put the toy on 9 and hop it back 4. Where does it land?

math.u02.sheet.03.title: Count on to add
math.u02.sheet.03.hint: Say 6, then count on two more: 7, 8.
math.u02.sheet.03.home: Hold up 6 fingers. Your child counts on 2 more to find 6 + 2.

math.u02.sheet.04.title: Count back to take away
math.u02.sheet.04.home: Put 8 spoons in a row. Take 3 away one at a time, counting back each time.

math.u02.sheet.05.title: Five and four more
math.u02.sheet.05.hint: Start at 5 and make four jumps forward.
math.u02.sheet.05.home: Play a board game: from square 5, move 4 squares and say where you land.

math.u02.sheet.06.title: Apple story
math.u02.sheet.06.hint: More apples join the group, so use plus.
math.u02.sheet.06.home: Tell a joining story with real fruit, then write its number sentence together.

math.u11.sheet.01.title: Back from 17
math.u11.sheet.01.home: Make a number line from 10 to 20 on the floor with tape. Your child stands on 17 and hops back 4.

math.u11.sheet.02.title: Jumps between
math.u11.sheet.02.hint: Count the jumps from 11 to 15, not the numbers.
math.u11.sheet.02.home: Put one finger on 11 and one on 15 on a ruler. Count the jumps between them together.

math.u11.sheet.03.title: Back from 16
math.u11.sheet.03.home: Count back from 16 together while taking away 3 small toys.

math.u11.sheet.04.title: Back from 19
math.u11.sheet.04.home: Practise counting back from 19 on the stairs, one step at a time.

math.u11.sheet.05.title: On from 12
math.u11.sheet.05.home: Your child says 12, then counts on 5 more with claps.

math.u11.sheet.06.title: Hopping story
math.u11.sheet.06.home: Play a hopping game on the floor number line and say the number sentence for each hop.

math.u14.sheet.01.title: On from 11
math.u14.sheet.01.home: On a number line from 10 to 20, your child starts on 11 and hops forward 5.

math.u14.sheet.02.title: Count on from 9
math.u14.sheet.02.home: Keep 9 in your heads and count on 6 claps together.

math.u14.sheet.03.title: Bigger number first
math.u14.sheet.03.hint: Start with 9, the bigger number, then count on 4.
math.u14.sheet.03.home: With two groups of toys, ask your child which number to start from to count on quickly.

math.u14.sheet.04.title: Start with 14
math.u14.sheet.04.hint: Which number is bigger, 3 or 14? Start there.
math.u14.sheet.04.home: Write 3 + 14 and 14 + 3. Talk about why both have the same answer.

math.u14.sheet.05.title: Double seven
math.u14.sheet.05.hint: Double means the same number twice: 7 and 7.
math.u14.sheet.05.home: Make two equal rows of 7 buttons and count them all.

math.u14.sheet.06.title: Skipping story
math.u14.sheet.06.hint: Before lunch and after lunch join together, so use plus.
math.u14.sheet.06.home: Count rope skips before and after a break, then write the number sentence together.

math.u08.book.01.title: Name the pentagon
math.u08.book.01.hint: Count the straight sides. A pentagon has 5.
math.u08.book.01.home: Draw a house: a square with a pointed roof. Count its 5 sides together. It is a pentagon.

math.u08.book.02.title: Hexagon sides
math.u08.book.02.hint: Touch each straight side once as you count.
math.u08.book.02.home: Look at a honeycomb picture or a hexagon nut. Count the 6 sides of one shape together.

math.u08.book.03.title: Above the table
math.u08.book.03.hint: Is the ball higher than the table top, or lower?
math.u08.book.03.home: Hold a toy above the table, then put it under the table. Your child says where it is each time.

math.u08.book.04.title: Under the table
math.u08.book.04.hint: Look at the table top. Is the ball over it or below it?
math.u08.book.04.home: Play hide and seek with a teddy: under the bed, under the table, under a chair. Say "under" each time.

math.u08.book.05.title: Behind the box
math.u08.book.05.hint: Part of the ball is hidden. What is hiding it?
math.u08.book.05.home: Put a ball behind a box, then in front of it. Your child says "behind" or "in front of".

math.u08.book.06.title: Squares on a grid
math.u08.book.06.hint: Find B along the bottom and 2 up the side. Then move up one square at a time.
math.u08.book.06.home: Draw a 4 by 4 grid with A to D along the bottom and 1 to 4 up the side. Move a coin and name its square.

math.u15.book.01.title: A tent shape
math.u15.book.01.hint: Look at the ends. Two triangles joined by rectangles make a prism.
math.u15.book.01.home: Fold a card into a tent. Count its faces together: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.

math.u15.book.02.title: Prism faces
math.u15.book.02.hint: Count the 2 triangle ends, then the 3 rectangle sides.
math.u15.book.02.home: Find a triangle-shaped chocolate box or make a paper tent. Put a sticker on each face as you count.

math.u15.book.03.title: Pyramid faces
math.u15.book.03.hint: Count 1 square at the bottom and 4 triangles on the sides.
math.u15.book.03.home: Look at a picture of the Pyramids of Giza. Count the square base and the 4 triangle sides.

math.u15.book.04.title: Turning shapes
math.u15.book.04.hint: Picture each shape turned onto its side. Does it look the same?
math.u15.book.04.home: Cut out a square and a long rectangle. Turn each a quarter turn and talk about which looks the same.

math.u15.book.05.title: Turn and move
math.u15.book.05.hint: Turn first. Then count the squares one at a time.
math.u15.book.05.home: Give your child instructions like a robot: turn right, 2 steps forwards. Then swap turns.

math.u15.book.06.title: Six sides
math.u15.book.06.hint: Count the sides of each shape. Which one has 6?
math.u15.book.06.home: Make shapes with straws or sticks: a triangle, a pentagon and a hexagon. Count the sides of each.

math.u16.book.01.title: Read the table
math.u16.book.01.hint: Find Bus in the first column. Read the number next to it.
math.u16.book.01.home: Ask the family how they travel to school or work. Write a table together and read it back.

math.u16.book.02.title: Most in the table
math.u16.book.02.hint: Look at the numbers. Which one is the largest?
math.u16.book.02.home: Make a table of the fruit at home. Ask which fruit there is most of.

math.u16.book.03.title: Count a list
math.u16.book.03.hint: Count the names next to Car, one at a time.
math.u16.book.03.home: Write a list of who likes tea and who likes juice. Count the names in each part.

math.u16.book.04.title: Table total
math.u16.book.04.hint: Add all the numbers in the table: 3 + 4 + 2 + 2.
math.u16.book.04.home: Count the cups, plates and spoons on the table. Write them in a table and add them up.

math.u18.book.01.title: How hot is it?
math.u18.book.01.hint: One tool has a red line that goes up when it is hot.
math.u18.book.01.home: Look at a thermometer together, or the temperature on a phone. Talk about hot and cold days.

math.u18.book.02.title: Measuring water
math.u18.book.02.hint: Which tool has a scale for water?
